gist: Zcash co-founder Sean and ZK researcher Dave walk through the Zcash roadmap: Tachyon's recursive-SNARK scaling and statelessness, a path from ~2.9 TPS toward 50k TPS needing ~100 MB/s, private information retrieval for wallets, three-pillar post-quantum migration, formal verification after an AI-found Orchard counterfeiting bug, and the fee-holding sustainability module and coin-holder governance. The thesis is that AI makes transparent ledgers unsafe and Zcash's narrow, privacy-maximalist design is the fix.

themes.theme: Privacy Urgency in the AI Era

insights.claim: AI has collapsed the cost of deanonymizing transparent ledgers: a teenager with an LLM can now cluster and track everyone on public chains, and free public databases of fully mined, quantified on-chain users are expected to appear.
insights.speaker: Sean (Zcash co-founder, Tachyon lead)
insights.so_what: Transparent-ledger users, not just criminals, become targets; supports demand for shielded money and privacy infrastructure.
insights.quote: a teenager just with access to an LLM basically uh can can identify and track everybody using these things

insights.claim: On-chain privacy risk compounds with every unrelated data leak (exchange breaches tie addresses to physical identity, balances single out individual whales), so the problem was always bad but only insiders with chain-analysis contacts could see it.
insights.speaker: Dave (ZK researcher, Osmosis co-founder)
insights.so_what: Each new breach retroactively de-anonymizes historical transparent activity.

insights.claim: Privacy interest in crypto exploded over the last year rather than improving gradually, which the speakers attribute to the AI resurgence making the threat obvious; they argue Zcash's decisions get copied industry-wide (e.g. the pairing curve choice Ethereum followed).
insights.speaker: Dave (ZK researcher, Osmosis co-founder)
insights.so_what: Zcash acts as the technical leader of crypto privacy; others follow its design choices.

insights.claim: Privacy raises the bar for phishing: attacks usually need to know which transaction to construct to steal funds, which requires a viewing key in Zcash, so shielded wallets are harder to phish.
insights.speaker: Dave (ZK researcher, Osmosis co-founder)
insights.so_what: A side benefit of shielding that is rarely priced in security comparisons.
insights.quote: cannot fish someone's wallet without a viewing key uh so easily.

insights.claim: Zcash's core philosophy is privacy maximalism measured by 'ledger indistinguishability': an adversary must be unable to tell two transactions apart, a much stronger bar than stealth addresses or ring signatures, which fail the game easily.
insights.speaker: Sean (Zcash co-founder, Tachyon lead)
insights.so_what: Gives a concrete test for ranking privacy chains; partial-privacy systems are structurally weaker.

insights.claim: Anything short of 100% privacy fails to set-intersection attacks: if a protocol anonymizes you among a large group each time, an attacker who sees just two transactions from the same target can quickly eliminate everyone else.
insights.speaker: Sean (Zcash co-founder, Tachyon lead)
insights.so_what: Large anonymity sets alone do not protect repeat users; leakage of any bits is fatal over time.

insights.claim: Zcash refuses any regulator backdoor or special viewing capability, and treats this as a values constraint rather than a negotiable design choice.
insights.speaker: Sean (Zcash co-founder, Tachyon lead)
insights.so_what: Regulatory-compliance privacy models (viewing keys for authorities) are a divergence point from Zcash.
insights.quote: We don't want to bend the knee on on the privacy uh stuff.

insights.claim: Inherited Bitcoin traits - 21 million hard cap and proof of work - are described as effectively settled for Zcash; changing them would need miners and coin holders on board.
insights.speaker: Dave (ZK researcher, Osmosis co-founder)
insights.so_what: Monetary policy and PoW are unlikely to change, so security-budget work must happen within them.

insights.claim: Zcash deliberately stayed narrow (no private DeFi, shielded assets or meme-coin features) because extra features enlarge the attack surface in a ZK system, where one subtle bug can break everything, and would have complicated the scaling upgrade; focus is payments first.
insights.speaker: Sean (Zcash co-founder, Tachyon lead)
insights.so_what: A deliberate bet against the Ethereum-style expressive-chain strategy; implies low odds of near-term Zcash DeFi.
insights.quote: we would be really screwed right now if we were trying to change the protocol to scale it

insights.claim: Dave sees only two expressivity gaps worth filling: richer custody (e.g. passkey/secp256r1 signing instead of off-chain MPC multisig) and trustless light-client bridges between chains; he would defer everything else until the chain handles far more than ~3 TPS.
insights.speaker: Dave (ZK researcher, Osmosis co-founder)
insights.so_what: Bridges and custody could improve cross-chain UX, but the roadmap is sequenced behind scaling.

insights.claim: Tachyon fixes two cryptographic scaling limits with recursive SNARKs: it aggregates per-transaction ZK proofs so a full node verifies one proof per block, and it removes the perpetually growing nullifier set (state bloat), making the chain effectively stateless.
insights.speaker: Sean (Zcash co-founder, Tachyon lead)
insights.so_what: Cryptography stops being the bottleneck, shifting the problem to consensus throughput and wallets.

insights.claim: Verifying one proof instead of a million is claimed to be roughly a 5x-plus scale improvement on day one, and the stateless design is a first-ever result co-developed by Sean and Ian Myers in a paper last year.
insights.speaker: Dave (ZK researcher, Osmosis co-founder)
insights.so_what: Tachyon is original research, not a port of Ethereum rollup tech.

insights.claim: Zcash is explicitly not optimizing for Raspberry Pi full nodes: a payment network targeting 50k TPS trades node accessibility for scale, with Dave agreeing Solana made the correct trade-off, though state removal cuts storage needs to a couple hundred GB of SSD.
insights.speaker: Dave (ZK researcher, Osmosis co-founder)
insights.so_what: Expect Zcash to accept heavier full nodes, in the opposite direction from Bitcoin's decentralization-first culture.

insights.claim: Today's Zcash chain processes about 60 KB/s with maximum capacity of ~2.9 TPS (about 6.5 TPS after the next upgrade); the 50k TPS goal at ~2 KB per transaction needs ~100 MB/s throughput. Near-term step is shorter block times (about 3x bandwidth, 60 to 180 KB/s), then erasure-coded blocks and better gossip as in Celestia and Solana.
insights.speaker: Dave (ZK researcher, Osmosis co-founder)
insights.so_what: Gives concrete targets for judging Zcash scaling progress: 1-10 MB/s is a straightforward path, 10-100 MB/s needs novel work.

insights.claim: Proof-of-work block-time variance becomes a hard constraint at higher speeds: at a 25-second average, about 1% of blocks arrive in ~250 ms and 1% take over 110 seconds, so sustaining throughput while keeping single-chain PoW security is the main open consensus problem over the next two years.
insights.speaker: Dave (ZK researcher, Osmosis co-founder)
insights.so_what: Fast PoW chains are untested at this scale; a failure here would cap Zcash throughput.

insights.claim: Receiving private payments requires wallets to discover payments without scanning the entire chain; Zcash is adopting private information retrieval (FHE-based queries over GPU-served matrix-vector math), already used for a coin-holder vote, so wallets can query a server without revealing what they want.
insights.speaker: Dave (ZK researcher, Osmosis co-founder)
insights.so_what: Wallet UX, not the ZK proof, was the real reason private-chain usability lagged; AI-driven GPU optimization is the enabler.

insights.claim: To avoid reliance on altruistic RPC providers, Zcash plans anonymous paid subscriptions: users mint one-time tokens and burn them with the same double-spend-proof technology, so providers verify payment without learning who is querying. Open engineering issues are onboarding and proof cost per query.
insights.speaker: Dave (ZK researcher, Osmosis co-founder)
insights.so_what: A private payments-for-infrastructure market avoids a foundation or state-funded dependency.

insights.claim: Zcash's post-quantum plan has three pillars: quantum recoverability (live now in the new shielded pool, so funds can be recovered after a quantum break), post-quantum privacy (via Tachyon, targeted for January next year, using ML-KEM-style key exchange), and post-quantum soundness (moving to recursive STARKs, so quantum computers cannot counterfeit).
insights.speaker: Sean (Zcash co-founder, Tachyon lead)
insights.so_what: Today a quantum computer could counterfeit shielded Zcash; the soundness migration is the final and hardest piece.

insights.claim: Intermediate steps are shipping early: the NEAR Intents integration is already quantum-unlinkable, and fully post-quantum transparent transactions plus a demo of freezing elliptic curves and moving from shielded to transparent are expected early to mid next year.
insights.speaker: Dave (ZK researcher, Osmosis co-founder)
insights.so_what: Observable milestones to track in 2027 for the quantum story.

insights.claim: Quantum panic is overstated for Zcash: an attacker would need exclusive quantum capability kept secret for a year-plus, would hit Bitcoin and Satoshi's coins first, and cannot target Zcash whales because balances are private.
insights.speaker: Sean (Zcash co-founder, Tachyon lead)
insights.so_what: Shielded pools get implicit 'bunker' protection that transparent chains lack.
insights.quote: I don't know who the whales are because it's private

insights.claim: Sean is skeptical of Justin Drake's 'bunker mode' alarm, arguing Ethereum has tied its technical identity to new cryptography, and that Drake may be pushing the Overton window as far as a doomer can go without looking ridiculous. He has seen no real examples of AI breaking classical crypto; the generous reading is that AI could accelerate quantum progress.
insights.speaker: Sean (Zcash co-founder, Tachyon lead)
insights.so_what: Treat the post-quantum urgency narrative as partly positioning by Ethereum; real AI attacks on crypto remain unproven.

insights.claim: An AI-found bug earlier this year in the Orchard shielded pool (a counterfeiting flaw) was the only such bug and so subtle only frontier AI found it, after auditors and cryptographers missed it for years; the response was a month-and-a-half sprint to formally verify the pool, shipping as the Ironwood pool.
insights.speaker: Sean (Zcash co-founder, Tachyon lead)
insights.so_what: AI-assisted bug hunting plus formal verification becomes the new security baseline for ZK chains.

insights.claim: Zcash audited the formal verification itself: ZK Security injected bug classes from a repository of roughly a thousand known ZK bugs and none escaped the proofs, which Sean believes is a first. Existing formal proofs also let the team check that Dave's proving optimizations kept zero-knowledge and quantify security bounds quickly.
insights.speaker: Sean (Zcash co-founder, Tachyon lead)
insights.so_what: Formal verification speeds optimization, not just assurance; other projects are asking to replicate it.

insights.claim: Dave expects AI-driven formal verification, including verifying compiled binaries for memory safety, to become the security story of the planet over the next two years, and wants to extend the method from cryptography to the full node.
insights.speaker: Dave (ZK researcher, Osmosis co-founder)
insights.so_what: Security tooling demand shifts toward formal methods plus AI fuzzing.
insights.quote: I think that's just going to be what the security story of the whole planet is next two years

insights.claim: Dave proposes multi-assumption security for the final shielded pool: combine two independent hash functions (e.g. BLAKE3 and SHA-2) or primitives so an attacker must break both, and raise soundness from 128 bits to 140-160. Sean is somewhat pessimistic because of the cost to scale; it is not consensus.
insights.speaker: Dave (ZK researcher, Osmosis co-founder)
insights.so_what: Defense-in-depth would trade proof size for resilience; adoption depends on scaling headroom.

insights.claim: Zcash's Network Sustainability Module holds 60% of transaction fees in the protocol starting November 5 and plans to redistribute them to miners beginning about four years later, pre-funding the long-run security budget while price is low.
insights.speaker: Dave (ZK researcher, Osmosis co-founder)
insights.so_what: A merged, dated change addressing the 21M-cap security-budget question; sufficiency remains an open question.

insights.claim: The long-term security budget is acknowledged as a real risk unlike Bitcoin maximalists' stance, but it is ranked below scale and speed in priority; Dave points to Bitcoin as the canary and notes the success case would let altruism supplement hashrate.
insights.speaker: Dave (ZK researcher, Osmosis co-founder)
insights.so_what: Security funding is a deferred rather than solved problem for fixed-supply PoW coins.

insights.claim: Governance has moved toward non-binding coin-holder votes (a roughly $7 million retroactive grant vote, and a large NU7 upgrade vote with millions of ZEC participating); the stated view is that strongly opposed holders should block a change, but votes cannot override core values.
insights.speaker: Sean (Zcash co-founder, Tachyon lead)
insights.so_what: Holder sentiment is becoming a de facto veto, adding a market-aligned check on developer-organization decisions.
insights.quote: It really matters what the Zack holders [music] think.

insights.claim: A high ZEC price is described as a prerequisite, not a side effect: demand for tens of thousands of TPS requires on the order of 100 million holders and a large market cap, and higher prices have already multiplied developer resources and community treasuries versus a few years ago.
insights.speaker: Dave (ZK researcher, Osmosis co-founder)
insights.so_what: Reflexivity: price funds development, which funds scale, which supports price.

insights.claim: Both speakers name governance stasis, via committees where progress equals the slowest member, as the biggest threat to Zcash, followed by tampering with monetary supply or governance's ability to compromise core values.
insights.speaker: Dave (ZK researcher, Osmosis co-founder)
insights.so_what: The attack surface they worry about is organizational, not cryptographic.
